notes: August 2026 cycle. Launch-on-login (LOL) desktop DAU tailwind (adjustment code `l`). CEILING = 200,000 DAU/day, selected 2026-07-29. This is the only LOL curve for this cycle: the earlier 125,000 / 165,000 / 180,000 variants were deleted 2026-07-30 (recoverable from git history; see launch_on_login/_index.md). Bidirectional overlay on legacy_desktop DAU: the historical rise is subtracted from modern_windows training rows before mozaic (allocated across countries by trailing 28d modern_windows DAU share), then the same curve is added back to the per-country forecast. Curve shape: zero before the 2026-05-08 rollout; rises with the measured holdback-experiment excess (FF152-excluded, interpolated 7d trailing MA) through the last clean day 2026-06-23, where it reads 130,296; then a linear ramp at 2,714/day (the recorded ~19,000/wk rise at the cutoff) reaching 200,000 and flat through 2027-12-31. The ceiling is first reached 2026-07-19, leaving only 9 plateau days inside the training window (which ends 2026-07-27) — so the last weeks of training see a rising subtraction rather than a flat one. MEASURED/EXTRAPOLATED BOUNDARY: everything after 2026-06-23 is extrapolation by construction — contamination begins 2026-06-24 when the holdback control received the feature, so the counterfactual is permanently gone and no telemetry can ever adjudicate the ceiling. Deleting the alternates removed the menu, not the uncertainty. CONSERVATISM: the measured effect had not plateaued at the cutoff (still rising ~19K/wk) and is held flat anyway; an independent convolution model of the same effect lands near 220,000/day, so 200,000 is only a ~20K/day haircut and is close to betting on that model rather than hedging against it. Changing the ceiling requires a new curve from the producer AND a model re-run — the curve is baked into the forecast parquet, so a spec-only edit changes nothing downstream. Curve produced by ~/work/launch-on-login/build_lol_tailwind.py (see model_meta_file for the exact invocation).
